key_insight: The paper introduces a unified analytical model that diagnoses where photoelectrochemical cell losses occur and turns that diagnosis into design guidance across different device architectures.
engineering_relevance: It gives engineers a quantitative way to compare materials and devices, identify bottlenecks from current-voltage data, and prioritize fixes like better interfaces, co-catalysts, or nanostructuring.
method: Unifies built-in junction and semiconductor-electrolyte junction photoelectrodes in one physically meaningful framework.
Generates current-voltage curves, efficiency metrics, and efficiency maps under ideal and realistic conditions.
Fits experimental I-V data to decompose losses into thermodynamic, optical, recombination, and interfacial contributions.
evidence_signal: The framework is validated against literature results across solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries, and it compares multiple absorber classes including Si, perovskites, hematite, and BiVO4.
watch_item: Model-based loss attribution depends on the quality of experimental I-V fits and may be sensitive to assumptions in parameterization for complex real devices.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
